A Bullion Trading Tradition
馬年 · 2026
Lunar New Year Gold — Year of the Horse 2026
Across the Chinese world, the weeks before Lunar New Year are among the busiest gold-buying days of the year — an auspicious way to “add to your wealth.” 2026 is the rare Year of the Fire Horse. Here is a plain-English guide to the customs, the numbers, and what to give.
Educational only — Lunar New Year is celebrated across Chinese, Vietnamese, Korean and other cultures; customs vary.

YEAR OF THE HORSE
Across the Chinese world, the weeks before
Lunar New Year
are among the busiest gold-buying days of the year. Red and gold are the colors of luck and joy, and buying or gifting gold is an auspicious way to “add to your wealth” and pass prosperity from one generation to the next. In 2026 the festival opens on
February 17
— the Year of the
Fire Horse
, a pairing that returns only once every sixty years.
If you’re sending an auspicious gift to family — a small gold coin for a child’s red envelope, a zodiac coin for someone born in a Horse year, or a Gold Panda for a collector — this is a plain-English guide to the customs, the numbers, and what to buy.

Why gold at Lunar New Year
Gold (
jīn
) symbolizes wealth, abundance, and “golden luck.” Elders traditionally give gold to younger generations to pass prosperity down the family line, and the God of Wealth,
Cai Shen
— pictured in red-and-gold robes holding gold ingots — is welcomed on the fifth day with open doors, incense, and firecrackers to invite fortune into homes and businesses for the year.
The most everyday expression is the
red envelope
—
hongbao
in Mandarin,
lai see
in Cantonese — which traditionally holds crisp new bills and, increasingly, a small gold coin or bar so the gift lasts. Zodiac gold has become the modern keepsake: the annually redesigned Gold and Silver Pandas, Year-of-the-Horse Lunar coins, and small gram bars that slip inside a red envelope.

A note on names.
“Lunar New Year” is the inclusive term — the holiday is celebrated by Chinese, Vietnamese (
Tết
), Korean (
Seollal
), and other communities, and customs differ. Much of the red-envelope and zodiac detail here is specifically Chinese (the Spring Festival). Vietnam’s Tết uses the Cat in place of the Rabbit and the Buffalo in place of the Ox; Korea’s Seollal is a quieter three-day rite centered on ancestral respect.
The twelve animals
The Chinese calendar pairs 12 zodiac animals with 5 elements, so any animal-and-element combination returns only once every 60 years. 2026 is the Horse — the seventh sign — carrying the element of Fire.

Red envelopes and lucky numbers
Red-envelope etiquette turns on
homophones
— words that sound like lucky (or unlucky) ideas. The number
8
(
fā
) sounds like “to prosper,” so amounts built on 8 are luckiest;
4
(
sì
) sounds like “death,” so any amount containing a 4 is avoided. Use crisp new bills, give and receive with both hands, and don’t open the envelope in front of the giver. Because a coin or bar rarely lands on a tidy lucky number, a graceful move is to pair the metal with a token lucky-number bill — an $8 or $88 note.

The Chinese Gold Panda
First struck in 1982, the Gold Panda was the first bullion coin to change its design
every year
— which is exactly what makes each one collectible. The obverse always shows the Temple of Heaven; the reverse shows a new panda annually. Since 2016 it has been minted in metric weights (1 g, 3 g, 8 g, 15 g, 30 g at .999 fine), and the small 1 g and 3 g coins fit neatly inside a red envelope.

Gold’s price has climbed sharply over the past decade, which only deepens both the gift meaning and the store-of-value case for a festival-timed coin. A year-specific piece — this year’s Horse, or the annual Panda — is a gift you can hold.

Common Questions
Questions families ask us
When is Lunar New Year 2026, and what animal is it?
It begins Tuesday, February 17, 2026 and the zodiac year runs to February 5, 2027. It is the Year of the Fire Horse — the Horse is the 7th of the 12 signs, and the Fire Horse pairing occurs only once every 60 years (last in 1966, next in 2086).
Why do people buy gold for Lunar New Year?
Gold symbolizes wealth, luck, and abundance, and red-and-gold are the festival’s colors. Buying or gifting gold is an auspicious way to “add to your wealth” for the year, and elders traditionally give gold to younger generations to pass prosperity down the family.
What’s the best small gold gift for a red envelope?
A 1 g or 3 g gold bar, or a 1 g/3 g Chinese Gold Panda (.999) — genuine 24K gold, small enough to tuck into a hongbao, and it holds real value. Pair it with a crisp lucky-number bill like $8 or $88 to honor both customs.
Why is 4 avoided and 8 preferred?
In Chinese, 4 (sì) sounds like the word for “death” (sǐ), so amounts like $4, $40, or $44 are unlucky. 8 (fā) sounds like “to make wealth,” making it the luckiest — which is why $88 and $888 are especially auspicious. Use even amounts and crisp new bills.
What is a Chinese Gold Panda?
A .999 fine gold bullion coin first issued by China’s official mint in 1982, famous for changing its panda design every single year. Since 2016 it’s minted in gram weights (1 g, 3 g, 8 g, 15 g, 30 g), with the Temple of Heaven on the obverse.
Should I buy this year’s animal, or the recipient’s birth animal?
Either is meaningful. This year’s Horse is a natural festival gift; a coin matching the recipient’s own birth-year animal (for the Horse: 1954, 1966, 1978, 1990, 2002, 2014, 2026) makes a personal milestone or birthday gift.
What’s the difference between .999 and .9999 gold?
Both are pure 24-karat gold. “.999” is 99.9% (“three nines”); “.9999” is 99.99% (“four nines”). Perth Mint and PAMP use .9999, the Panda uses .999 — for a gift there is no meaningful value difference.
What’s a good affordable Lunar New Year gift?
Silver is the accessible tier. A 1 oz Year of the Horse silver coin or a 30 g Silver Panda (.999) typically lands around $60–$120 delivered — a real precious-metal gift with strong cultural meaning at a fraction of a gold piece’s cost.
Is Chinese New Year the same as Vietnamese Tết and Korean Seollal?
They share the lunar calendar but differ. Vietnam’s Tết uses the Cat in place of the Rabbit and the Buffalo in place of the Ox. Korea’s Seollal is a quieter three-day observance centered on ancestral rites. China’s Spring Festival is the longest, about 15 days.
Gifting for the Year of the Horse?
Lunar New Year 2026 is February 17. Order early so your Year-of-the-Horse coin, Gold Panda, or a small gold bar for a red envelope arrives in time — we ship nationwide and can help you match a piece to each recipient.
